setup-terminal.def: The Mac app where you control the computer by typing commands instead of clicking.

setup-prompt.def: The text Terminal shows when it is ready for a command, e.g. you@MacBook-Air ~ %: user, computer, current folder, then %.

setup-shell.def: The program inside Terminal that reads and runs your commands. On a Mac it is zsh.

setup-path.def: The list of folders from the top of the disk down to a place, joined by slashes, e.g. /Users/you/ml-course. ~ is your home folder, .. the folder above.

setup-flag.def: Extra words starting with dashes that change what a command does, e.g. --version or -a.

setup-uv.def: A fast tool that downloads Python, creates virtual environments and installs libraries (uv venv, uv pip install).

setup-pipe.def: Sends the output of the command on its left into the command on its right.

setup-path-var.def: The list of folders the shell searches when you type a program's name. Activating a .venv puts its bin folder first.

setup-venv.def: A private, self-contained copy of Python plus libraries for one project, stored in a folder (here ~/ml-course/.venv).

setup-activate.def: source .venv/bin/activate: makes this Terminal window use the environment's Python. The prompt then starts with (.venv).

setup-library.def: Code written and shared by others that you install and import, e.g. numpy, pandas, scikit-learn.

setup-mps.def: Metal Performance Shaders: lets PyTorch use the GPU of an Apple Silicon Mac (device="mps").

setup-vscode.def: Visual Studio Code, a free code editor; with the Python and Jupyter extensions it runs notebooks.

setup-notebook.def: A document of text cells and code cells; each code cell's output appears under it.

setup-kernel.def: The Python program that runs a notebook's cells. Pick the .venv one so the notebook sees your libraries.
